blocks.html:
Welcome to OneAccord! Over the next 12 weeks you'll pick up where Discovery Day left off and turn what you learned into a working practice. This course helps you:

  • Get your business off the ground with a clear structure
  • Build the right habits early (and avoid costly ones) so your practice becomes sustainable quickly
  • Build real relationships with your fellow OneAccord Principals

The assignments are based on what we know works. Set aside time every week and treat this training with the same priority as building your network.

How each week works

  1. Lessons: short videos and key points, with a few quick checks and a practice scenario your AI coach grades.
  2. Field assignments: real conversations with referral partners, prospects and fellow Principals, observed by someone who gives you feedback.
  3. Check-in: at the end of each week you answer a few reflection questions. They save to your Coaching Journal.
  4. Coaching call: download your journal and review it with your coach in a weekly 30-minute call. Calls start after Week 1.

blocks.html:
Who we are

OneAccord's brand promise is simple: We make companies more valuable. Our values, Service, Compassion and Truth, shape how we treat clients, partners and each other. Whether you're an Associate, Principal or Partner, you deliver on that promise.

Referral networks are how we reach more of the businesses that need us. Building them is a natural extension of service: you help partners serve their clients, and they introduce you to owners you could never reach alone.

blocks.html:
Your three ongoing assignments

Each week you'll have one or two field assignments. Here's the full picture; each week gives you that week's focus.

Team Integration (Weeks 1-5)

Meet one new Principal each week. Knowing your colleagues' strengths makes you more valuable to referral partners and clients: you bring your network and theirs, you can pass opportunities that don't fit you (earning lead fees), and the right Principals help you land and expand engagements you couldn't alone. It's also how you join a community of like-minded people.

Developing Your Referral Network (Weeks 1-4 and 9-12)

Referral development is the most valuable part of your practice: the engine of your business, the source of your stability and control, and a revenue stream in itself. You'll hold four referral conversations in each round, each observed by a fellow Principal, a peer, or the partner themselves, who fills out the evaluation form. You choose which meetings get evaluated. And remember: the best leaders ask for feedback.

Prospect Discovery (Weeks 5-8)

Principals who are good at developing prospects earn through direct work and lead fees. These skills can be taught; success is as much about persona as persistence. You'll hold four practice discovery conversations with CEOs, with feedback each time.

blocks.html:
Working with your coach

Your coach is a Managing Principal assigned to you for these 12 weeks. They're here to help you get the most out of the course: a sounding board and mentor. They are not a judge, so you have nothing to prove.

The bar to join OneAccord is high, and we believe you want it that way. We're looking for people who invest in the process: engage, do the work, and see the 12 weeks through. Let's grow!

blocks.label: The coaching agreement
blocks.instructions:
As the participant: I'm excited to grow in my role at OneAccord, engage with the material and apply it to my work. I commit to a growth mindset and to being punctual and prepared for our meetings. I'm responsible for my choices about what actions to take and what we work on together.

Your coach commits: to partner with you, be punctual and prepared, be honest and open, and handle what you share with respect and discretion.

Practical expectations: weekly 30-minute check-ins for the 12 weeks; keep rescheduling and cancellations to a minimum; if you can't make a meeting, tell your coach and reschedule with as much notice as possible (24 hours minimum).

blocks.coachContext: Course structure: an Introduction plus Weeks 1-12. Each week has short lessons with a video, field assignments, a weekly check-in the learner writes into their Coaching Journal, and a 30-minute weekly call with their coach (an assigned Managing Principal). Ongoing field assignments: Team Integration (weeks 1-5: meet a new OneAccord Principal each week and learn their industry experience, where their contacts are, core strengths, and why you'd bring them into a conversation); Developing Your Referral Network (weeks 1-4 and 9-12: four referral-partner conversations per round, each observed by someone who completes the OA Principal Evaluation Form; meeting 1 explores a new partner's needs and goals, meeting 2 deepens the relationship and shares what you do, meeting 3 clarifies when and how they'd refer (referral criteria, a smooth process, your 'work product'), meeting 4 opens a new partner and sets up regular interaction); Prospect Discovery (weeks 5-8: practice discovery conversations with a CEO connection who names one need in advance; the aim is to investigate, not sell, focusing on the questions you ask and relating as an advisor/mentor; the next step is a Client Success Plan or a brief revenue review; if no CEO is available, role-play a case study). Goal: at least eight referral-partner appointments over the course. Referral partners include CPAs, wealth advisors, M&A advisors, bankers, attorneys and others who see owners at every stage (starting, scaling, exiting). Referral network development is the engine of a principal's practice: the source of stability and control, and a revenue stream itself through lead fees. Key ideas: owner dependency is usually the top risk discounting a private company's value (often 10-30%); in the 'Value of Your Business' example a company with $1M sustainable EBITDA at a 5x multiple is worth a potential $5M, a 20% owner-dependency discount takes it to $4M, and other risks (customer concentration, weak pipeline, poor financials, thin management) plus an earn-out can leave about $3M at closing; earn-outs are contingent payments the seller no longer controls. Team: Principals each run a self-sufficient practice but bring in fellow Principals with complementary strengths (1+1=3), pass leads that don't fit (lead fees), and lean on OneAccord's brand, IP and resources. OneAccord serves both sellers (increase value before a sale) and buyers (evaluate and improve an acquisition). Eight components of a practice: client-specific (referral network development, prospect discovery, structuring engagements, client delivery and communication) and practice-specific (practice balance, team involvement, regional goals, corporate standards and best practices). Case studies: Redden Marine (stuck sales, chaos, low morale; working contract for the leadership team, SOPs, hiring and onboarding, one-on-ones, monthly all-hands; revenue about $21M to just under $27M, net income +61%, morale from below 1 to over 4 on a 5-point scale); EZ Lube (turnaround after Chapter 11; trained the district managers rather than technicians; 18-month sales goals met in five months; sold to Valvoline, which rehired every DM); Redfern Concrete (family succession; separate then shared objectives; brought in CPA, attorney and wealth advisor; sale price up 70%, lower taxes, manageable payments for the son); Critical Power (founder bought assets of a business losing $1M a year; OneAccord as fractional COO; culture, training, one-page plan; revenue +$5M and profits tripled in year two); Breakwater Security (revenue realignment: roles, metrics, compensation, sales strategy, inside sales and channels; led to the desired valuation and acquisition).
